projects.title: Collections analytics & automation
projects.when: December 2016 to September 2025. Analyst I to Analyst III, Collection Intelligence/Contribution Recovery.
projects.summary: Power BI reporting, SQL pipelines and automations for the collections team at Sura Peru (AFP Integra).
projects.problem: Each debt report took ~30 minutes to produce. The late-payment rate was 27%. Some of the 5 external collection providers I supervised were redundant.
projects.built: I built Power BI dashboards, SQL data pipelines (DB2, BigQuery) and workflows in Excel/VBA and Power Automate.

results.label: late-payment rate
results.text: I lowered the late-payment rate from 27% to 24% by pairing the scoring model with targeted campaigns.

results.label: lower operating costs
results.text: I cut operating costs ~40% by using scoring and performance data to consolidate the redundant external providers I supervised (from a panel of 5).

results.label: per report
results.text: I cut debt-report generation from ~30 minutes to ~2 minutes per report with Excel VBA and Access macros. That also made batch generation possible.

results.label: less manual processing
results.text: I reduced manual processing ~45% across the team with automations and standardized, parameter-driven reports, including self-service report tools for the legal team.

ai.used: I used generative AI to speed up writing complex BigQuery SQL.

projects.summary: A Python agent that flags likely occupation mis-codes in Job Bank postings for review.
projects.measure: Triage time by hand vs with the agent.

projects.title: Bike Share Toronto rebalancing optimizer
projects.summary: A station demand forecast plus a mixed-integer model for rebalancing bikes between stations.
projects.details: The model runs on Gurobi and can be rerun with an open solver. I compare it with no rebalancing and with a greedy heuristic. Results are labelled "modelled".
